annotations.title: Match a precise sighting to a satellite

description: Check whether a precisely measured point in the sky (azimuth, elevation and exact time) matches one of about 160 bright satellites and rocket bodies within 2 degrees, also listing planets, the Moon and bright stars within 5 degrees. Use it when the witness measured the direction (compass, phone app); for a vague memory ('a light last night towards the west') use what_did_i_see, for a fixed star or planet use which_star. Returns insufficient_data when orbital elements are older than 72 hours. A match means compatible with the observation, not proven; the tool never says 'UFO detected'.

az.description: Direction in degrees from true north, clockwise: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west.

el.description: Height above the horizon in degrees: 0 = horizon, 90 = straight overhead.

lang.description: Language of the text fields: fr (default) or en.

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (north positive).

lng.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

time.description: Moment of the observation, ISO-8601 with a time zone, e.g. 2026-11-01T19:30:00Z.

name: identify

outputSchema.description: Returns verdict (compatible | no_catalog_match | insufficient_data), answer, best_match, matches, natural_objects_within_5deg, rejected_matches, separation_deg.

title: Match a precise sighting to a satellite
